subject: RRO plans & version name in download package name

messages.author: 2ef256a129b97763
messages.subject: RRO plans & version name in download package name
parts:
I wonder what are the plans for RRO?  Currently the installer file name says "8 beta".  I assume there will soon be a "8 GA version" and possibly soon another 9 beta (for 3.12). 

I would also recommend more clarity (including in mentioning either publication date or sub-version release number in the installer: I know that since RRO has been made available you have already made a number of changes but the name has been kept the same).

Part of the reason for my questions is that I am interested in using RRO in a commercial project.  Initially the plan is to use plain open source R, but I expect soon there will be a requirement for a supported version of R.

Adopting RRO I understand that I could do the above keeping the same code base.  If I use CRAN R (beside the fundamental lack of intel MKL) I would have a (slightly) different code base: this would save me to budget for a test / regression test of the application (no need as the code would be identical).

Kindly confirm if I understand the above correctly. Thanks

messages.author: 88275a537c4bd7d2
messages.subject: Re: RRO plans & version name in download package name
parts:
Hi Enzo,

We plan to keep the "beta" label for the next couple of months as we get feedback from the field. We will continue to release new versions even while it's in beta though, and yes, new versions will all have distinct version numbers :). The next version will be 8.0.1 beta, based on R 3.1.2.

We already provide support for Revolution R Open (even in its beta state) through the Revolution R Plus program.

Cheers,
# David Smith
